dropped.note: Hex/mixed BSD IPv4 forms such as http://0x7f.1:8081 or http://127.0.0.0x1 contain a letter, so isHostName (TargetUrl.java:136-150) takes them as names, while the all-digit guard refuses 127.1 and 4294967295. Whether InetSocketAddress then reaches 127.0.0.1 depends on the platform resolver: inet_aton reads it as 127.0.0.1, but recent JDK updates refuse ambiguous literals by default (jdk.net.allowAmbiguousIPAddressLiterals). I could not show a wrong outcome without a driver program, which the review rules forbid. The SRS/D-048 also leave the name grammar open, the URL comes from the developer and not from a client, and the Host header carries the string as written. Dropped as unproven.

Request-line and Host smuggling: the authority holds only [A-Za-z0-9._-] names, a port of digits, or an IPv6 literal that isIpv6 checks for hex digits, colons and a dotted tail; ']' must be followed by end or ':'+digits; '@', '%', '\\', space and controls are refused. The base path goes through PathChecker.isSafePath (no 0x00-0x20, 0x7F, non-ASCII, '#', bad '%', encoded unreserved, '/', '\\', NUL, or %25 double encoding), and '?' is refused for the whole URL. I found no string that injects CR/LF, a space or a second authority into the backend request line (Proxy.java:443) or Host (target.authority).

Hosts like '-', 'a..b' and '.h' and ports with leading zeros ('h:00080') are accepted. D-048 does not define the name grammar, and RFC 3986 allows port *DIGIT. An odd name only gives an unresolved connect (a backend failure), not a different host. How the Host header carries the authority belongs to FR-PROXY-004, out of scope. Dropped.
http://[::] (unspecified address) is accepted. It is a valid RFC 4291 literal that the developer configures, and D-048 does not exclude it. Dropped.

TargetUrl.hostLiteral and TargetUrl.isDefaultPort() have no caller in NaruServe-proxy/src (grep). They look prepared for FR-PROXY-004 (Host header), which is out of scope here, and they cause no wrong behavior. Dropped as style or forward-looking.

Proxy.to's public javadoc uses {@link TargetUrl}, a package-private class. Whether javadoc (withJavadocJar runs in build) warns or fails could not be checked with the one Gradle command allowed. The other comments match the code: the TargetUrl class/field/method docs, the parsePort sign claim, the isIpv4 'no leading zeros', the isIpv6 grammar, and PathChecker's mention of Proxy.to applying isSafePath. Dropped as unproven.

AC-1..AC-6 each have dedicated tests: AC-1 has 5 tests covering every listed example; AC-2 has accepted forms via describe(), zone id, non-ASCII, ports 0/65536/abc, not-a-URL, plus an IPv6 connect test; AC-3 and AC-4 check the request line at a recording backend under /api/orders; AC-5 has all five SRS examples plus more; AC-6 expects NPE. Mutants I tried by hand (strip one trailing slash only, accept empty port, accept query or fragment, accept zone id, NPE→IAE, lastIndexOf port split) each fail at least one test.

The IPv6 connect test is skipped through Assume when ::1 cannot be bound, so on such hosts the brackets-stripped connect is not exercised. This is acceptable, and no flakiness was found: ephemeral ports, closeables and apps are torn down in @After, and the acceptor thread is a daemon that stops when the socket closes. Gradle run: ProxyTargetUrlTest tests=24 failures=0 errors=0 skipped=0 (task UP-TO-DATE against the current sources).
TargetUrl is immutable, with final fields and no shared state. Every refusal throws IllegalArgumentException at Proxy.to, and null throws NullPointerException before any other check. Nothing found.

summary: FR-PROXY-001 review, round 1: 0 kept findings. TargetUrl.parse follows the SRS: http/https in any case, a name, IPv4 dotted-quad or bracketed IPv6 host with no zone id, a port of 1..65535 in ASCII digits only, every trailing slash removed, the base path checked with PathChecker.isSafePath, IllegalArgumentException for a query, fragment, user info, another scheme or no host, and NullPointerException for null. This also matches D-048/D-072 and the hand-parsing Implementation Note. The Proxy public API is unchanged (to(String) has the same signature). No request-line or Host smuggling path was found. Tests cover AC-1..AC-6 with assertions that a wrong implementation fails; the Gradle run shows 24/24 passing, 0 skipped. Dropped as unproven or out of scope: hex IPv4 hosts (resolver-dependent), the dead members hostLiteral and isDefaultPort, and the javadoc link to a package-private class.
